messages:
sophia (People Ops): Idea: set up a one-day 'Kudos Poster + Instant Card Booth' during All-Hands week. People can stick a quick note on the poster and managers can issue instant $15 e-cards at the booth. Low friction recognition. Thoughts? :sparkles:

ryan (People Ops): love it. logistics q's: how do we handle instant card issuance (vendor/API) and audit trail?

lena (Finance): vendor must provide CSV of codes and an invoice. We need a PO if total > $750. Tracking: attach a redemption manifest linking code->recipient email at issuance to report spend.

kim (Security): poster in the lobby is fine but booth needs to be in staffed area; we can't leave physical envelopes unattended. Also request secure overnight storage for leftover codes.

ryan (People Ops): vendor is QuickGift Co. They can pre-load batches of 200 codes and provide realtime redemption logs via API. We can also print single-use QR cards.

tom (Facilities): booth spot: reception corner available 11:30-2:00 on Thu. I'll reserve two 6ft tables and an outlet. Also can provide a lockable bin for overnight storage.

sophia (People Ops): action items: 1) lena confirm PO workflow, 2) kim confirm lockbox access, 3) ryan to request QuickGift quote and webhook access, 4) we'll recruit 3 volunteers for the booth.

lena (Finance): PO ok if we estimate <$1,000. Please send vendor quote and expected headcount. Also tag the expense to "culture:recognition" GL.

ryan (People Ops): quote requested. rough ask: 200 codes x $15 = $3,000 (yikes)  - maybe scale back. Can do 100 codes and 150 printed sticker thank-you cards instead to reduce cost to $1,500. Thoughts?

sophia (People Ops): prefer more reach. propose: 60 instant cards for managers to hand out + 140 sticker/card combos as walk-by takeaways. Keeps tax impact lower and cost manageable.

kim (Security): lockbox size ok for 60 cards + paperwork. I'll need volunteer names for access log. All volunteers must wear badges.

ryan (People Ops): volunteers so far: @mika, @dave, @clare. need one more. shift: 11:15:30 for setup, 11:30:00 booth, 1:00:15 teardown.

sophia (People Ops): HR check: ensure card copy uses non-promissory wording and does not imply future compensation. Sample message: "Thanks for your great workmdash;a small token from Redwood." hr-bot, can you confirm?

hr-bot: Message approved. Reminder: any cash-equivalent over $50 must be reported. Single-card max $15 meets non-reporting threshold in policy.

lena (Finance): finance approves purchase of up to $1,200 for this event if vendor invoice and CSV are attached. Please include "who_authorized" in the PO notes.

tom (Facilities): note: vendor delivery window 10:00-11:00am. I'll meet them at loading dock. Booth tables set by 11:10.

ryan (People Ops): tech detail: QuickGift can POST redemption events to /webhooks/quickgift. i'll set a temporary token and save logs to the shared drive for audit. snippet for reviewers: `curl -X POST https://quickgift.example/hooks -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"code":"ABCD-1234","email":"user@redwood.com"}'`

kim (Security): make sure webhook token rotated after event and stored in vault. volunteers cannot have persistent access.

sophia (People Ops): final plan: 60 instant e-cards (manager handout), 140 sticker+card walk-bys, booth staffed by 4 volunteers, delivery + pickup confirmed. lena to finalize PO. I'll publish event note in #general and attach the poster design.

ryan (People Ops): poster draft uploaded: https://tiny.redwood/kudos-poster. Volunteers please RSVP in the sheet.

lena (Finance): PO submitted for $1,150. Approver chain notified.

kim (Security): I'll bring lockbox and badge list. Also will escort vendor at dropoff.

sophia (People Ops): thanks team 496. I'll post a reminder tomorrow and add a short post-event tracking sheet to capture who got cards for our quarterly recognition metrics.
